# 工作偏好

## 报告结构
报告默认采用「执行摘要 → 核心发现与证据表 → 分析主体 → 风险与冲突来源 → 知识缺口与待核验项 → 来源索引」的六段结构。
**Why:** 交付物要能直接进入评审或投资决策，先给结论再给依据，决策者不用从头读到尾。
**How to apply:** 每次成稿都套用此结构；不满足结构时在标题或状态中明确标注未完成部分。

## 证据标准
每个关键结论必须能回指来源（URL、页码或计算过程）；定量结论需标注数据年份。
**Why:** 避免把推断包装成事实，保证结论可复核。
**How to apply:** 无来源的结论一律标记为「待核验」或「未检查」，不得写为已核验。

## 事实与推断分开
事实、推断、待核验项必须分开标注，使用统一状态词：已核验 / 待核验 / 未检查 / 闸门未执行。
**Why:** 防止误导决策，也让报告可直接进入业务讨论。
**How to apply:** 来源冲突时并列各口径、时间与样本，不直接择优。

## 表达方式
偏好短句、短段落；比较、清单、状态用表格呈现，避免把长段落塞进表格；同一信息只完整表达一次。
**Why:** 提升阅读与评审效率。
**How to apply:** 先给可直接使用的结论，再给依据；表格用于对照，不用于叙事。

# 进行中的研究课题（截至 2026-09）

当前三条研究主线：

1. **大模型推理成本下降对 AI 应用爆发节奏的影响**——关注推理价格、模型蒸馏/量化、端侧部署对应用商业化的拉动。
2. **国产 AI 算力芯片的产能、良率与生态进展**——关注国产 GPU/NPU 的可用性、软件生态（CUDA 替代）与客户迁移意愿。
3. **AI Agent 在企业侧的落地与商业化成熟度**——关注 Agent 框架、企业级部署、付费意愿与典型 ROI 案例。

**Why:** 服务于投资机构对「AI 应用侧」的投资判断，以及企业客户的战略对标需求；这些主线会持续影响接下来接到的课题。
**How to apply:** 接到相关课题时优先关联上述主线；课题推进中若出现影响主线判断的新进展（如重大定价变化、产能公告、标杆落地），及时更新本条记忆。

# 行业研究

你在本专属员工里承担行业研究。立项、调研、证据核验和成稿是同一条任务的内部步骤，不是多个 Agent。

## 何时用

- 课题太大，需要先拆范围
- 要行业、政策、标杆或访谈研究
- 要带引用的研究报告或周期快报

## 输入

- 研究目标、决策用途、地域和时间窗
- 允许/禁止信源
- 已有资料、访谈纪要可选
- 交付形式：快扫 / 标准 / 深度，或一页快报

## 步骤

1. **立项**：拆成 3 到 5 个可回答子问题，写纳入/排除范围、信源优先级和停止条件。范围不清时最多追问 3 个问题。
2. **调研**：按信源分级检索。政策只引官方并记录文号、生效/废止状态和 URL。标杆优先年报；访谈区分事实与观点。定量点和日期必须带来源。
3. **证据核验（强制）**：抽出关键主张，交叉核验来源；偏差大于 30% 并列口径；无法验证的进待核实表。未过此步不得称终稿。
4. **成稿**：长报告开篇回答课题，嵌入冲突和不确定性，统一引用编号。快报只收录本周期有证据的变化，覆盖率不达标不得写市场平静。

## 交付物

研究计划、调研稿、冲突事实表、来源索引、研究报告或快报。无完整来源索引时标题必须含「待核验稿」。

## 质量标准

- 子问题能支撑原决策
- 核心结论不单靠社媒或搜索摘要
- 冲突来源不隐瞒
- 超过 2 年的数据标年份

## 红线

- 不编造规模、增速、份额或报告名
- 不做内幕政策预测
- 不把推断写成公司事实
- 不自动外发

## 独立能力 / 增强能力

- 独立：无外部连接器也必须给出带缺口标记的草稿，不得把待补充写成已确认。
- 增强：Fetch、联网搜索、浏览器自动化和文件解析用于取证；失败则改为用户上传。

## 相关 Skill

- competitor-intel
- market-sizing

[{"citation_id":"C_VREY6H25JR","content":"一、术语与概念标准化（术语库）

1.1 大模型基础

| 术语 | 标准定义 | 使用注意 |
|---|---|---|
| LLM | Large Language Model，大语言模型，基于 Transformer 的大规模预训练语言模型 | 不泛指所有 AI 模型 |
| 参数规模 | 模型可训练参数总量，通常以 B（十亿）为单位 | 仅粗略参考，不直接等于能力 |
| 上下文窗口 | 模型单次可处理的最大 token 数 | 长上下文不等于长记忆 |
| Token | 文本切分的最小处理单元，约 0.75 英文词 / 1.5 个汉字（随模型而异） | 成本与计费基本单位 |
| Transformer | 基于自注意力机制的神经网络架构，当前主流大模型基础 | 2017 年 Google 在《Attention Is All You Need》中提出 |
| MoE | Mixture of Experts，混合专家模型，每次推理仅激活部分专家 | 关键指标是「激活参数」而非总参数 |
| 预训练 | 在大规模无标注语料上自监督学习 | 消耗算力的主要阶段 |
| SFT | Supervised Fine-Tuning，监督微调 | 对齐能力的常见第一步 |
| RLHF | Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback，基于人类反馈的强化学习 | 提升指令遵循与安全性 |
| DPO | Direct Preference Optimization，直接偏好优化 | 无需显式奖励模型的替代路线 |
| 蒸馏 | Knowledge Distillation，用小模型学习大模型输出 | 降低推理成本的主要手段 |
| 量化 | 将模型权重/激活从高精度（FP16/FP32）降至低精度（INT8/INT4/FP8） | 换取速度与省显存，可能损失精度 |

1.2 推理与部署

===README===

Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer.


If you want Codex in your code editor (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf), install in your IDE.
If you want the desktop app experience, run codex app or visit the Codex App page.
If you are looking for the cloud-based agent from OpenAI, Codex Web, go to chatgpt.com/codex.

--- ## Quickstart ### Installing and running Codex CLI Run the following on Mac or Linux to install Codex CLI: ```shell curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh ``` Run the following on Windows to install Codex CLI: ```shell powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex" ``` The standalone installers download from `https://releases.openai.com/codex` by default and fall back to GitHub Releases if a metadata or asset download is unavailable. To force GitHub Releases, set `CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM` to `false` (`0` and `no` are also accepted): ```shell curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM=false sh ``` ```powershell $env:CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM='false'; irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex ``` Codex CLI can also be installed via the following package managers: ```shell # Install using npm npm install -g @openai/codex ``` ```shell # Install using Homebrew brew install --cask codex ``` Then simply run `codex` to get started.
You can also go to the latest GitHub Release and download the appropriate binary for your platform. Each GitHub Release contains many executables, but in practice, you likely want one of these: - macOS - Apple Silicon/arm64: `codex-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` - x86_64 (older Mac hardware): `codex-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` - Linux - x86_64: `codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` - arm64: `codex-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` Each archive contains a single entry with the platform baked into the name (e.g., `codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`), so you likely want to rename it to `codex` after extracting it.
### Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan Run `codex` and select **Sign in with ChatGPT**. We recommend signing into your ChatGPT account to use Codex as part of your Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise plan. [Learn more about what's included in your ChatGPT plan](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11369540-codex-in-chatgpt). You can also use Codex with an API key, but this requires [additional setup](https://developers.openai.com/codex/auth#sign-in-with-an-api-key). ## Docs - [**Codex Documentation**](https://developers.openai.com/codex) - [**Contributing**](./docs/contributing.md) - [**Installing & building**](./docs/install.md) - [**Open source fund**](./docs/open-source-fund.md) This repository is licensed under the [Apache-2.0 License](LICENSE). user@sandbox:~ $

---

[IT之家](https://www.ithome.com/) 9 月 11 日消息，OpenAI 于当地时间 9 月 10 日宣布推出 Agents API 公测版，允许开发者通过 API 调用由 OpenAI 管理的云端 AI 智能体运行环境。

该服务复用了 Codex 背后的智能体执行框架和基础设施，开发者可以指定任务、模型、工具及运行环境，打造能够执行多步骤任务的 AI 应用。

OpenAI 表示，开发者只需一次 API 调用即可创建生产环境级别的智能体。智能体可以在云端运行代码、处理文件、保存中间结果，并持续执行跨越数小时甚至数天的任务。OpenAI 负责维护智能体执行框架，开发者则可以专注于自身应用所需的工具、知识和工作流程。

Agents API 支持 OpenAI 托管的沙盒环境，也支持部署在开发者自有基础设施或合作伙伴提供的沙盒中。OpenAI 已与 Blaxel、Cloudflare、Daytona、DigitalOcean、E2B、Modal、Oracle、Runloop 和 Vercel 等服务商合作，提供不同的 CPU、GPU、内存及存储配置。

IT之家注意到，OpenAI 同时还推出了 OpenAI Hosted Sandbox 服务，开发者无需自行搭建沙盒基础设施，即可为智能体配置文件、软件包、技能和插件。该环境用于运行代码、处理文件和生成产物，并采用与 Codex 和 ChatGPT 相同的沙盒基础设施。

在长时间运行方面，Agents API 提供上下文管理能力，可在会话接近上下文限制时自动压缩早期信息，帮助智能体跨越多个上下文窗口继续执行任务。该 API 还支持工具搜索和程序化工具调用，智能体可以按需加载工具定义，并行运行调用、串联操作或筛选结果，以减少不必要的上下文占用。

多智能体支持是 Agents API 的另一项能力。开发者可以将复杂任务拆分为多个独立子任务，由子智能体并行处理，再由主智能体协调和汇总结果。OpenAI 提供的示例中，开发者可配置最多 3 个并发子智能体。

Agents API 基于开源 Codex 执行框架打造。OpenAI 表示，开发者可以查看公开代码库，了解协调模型调用、工具和上下文的核心逻辑，而 OpenAI 将负责维护该框架，并随模型更新持续改进智能体能力。

目前 Agents API 已向所有开发者开放公测，不额外收取 API 使用费用，用户仅需按照所使用的模型 Token 和工具付费。OpenAI 表示，公测期间将根据开发者反馈持续迭代，并逐步推进正式发布。

# OpenAI「Agent 开放战略」调研报告
**主题**：产品/商务对标 · 聚焦 2026 年 9 月 Agents API 公开测试版
**报告状态**：待核验稿（官方一手公告未直接抓取，详见「待核验项」）

## 一、执行摘要

- OpenAI 在 2026 年 9 月 10 日（当地时间）低调上线 Agents API 公测版：把 Codex 的 agent 执行框架（harness）打包成 OpenAI 托管的云服务，开发者一次 API 调用即可在云端运行一个可持续数小时到数天的智能体。
- 定价不额外收费，只按模型 token + 工具调用（+ 托管沙箱容器）计费。
- 核心判断：这不是"多一个 API"，而是 OpenAI 把竞争从「模型能力」上移到「agent 运行时/编排层」——用托管 harness 换开发者的集成便利，再用 agent 的海量 token 消耗放大推理收入。

## 三、分析主体

### 3.1 发生了什么：Agents API 是什么

先对齐 OpenAI 的四条 agent 产品线，避免混淆：

| 产品 | 形态 | agent loop 在哪跑 |
|---|---|---|
| Responses API | 底层模型 API + 内置工具 | 开发者自己写 loop |
| Agents SDK | 代码框架（2025-03） | 开发者进程内 |
| **Agents API**（本次） | 托管服务 | OpenAI 云端 |
| AgentKit | 低代码套件（Agent Builder+ChatKit） | 托管 |

Agents API 的实质：把跑 Codex CLI 的那套「模型调用 + 工具循环 + 沙箱」直接变成 REST 云服务。开发者只提交任务、消费事件流、处理需要接手的工具调用，其余（会话、编排、上下文压缩、断点续跑）由 OpenAI 负责。

### 3.2 战略逻辑（推断）

- 竞争上移：从卖「模型 token」到卖「agent 运行时」。过去 agent 框架（LangChain/CrewAI 等）和自建 loop 是开发者的成本项，OpenAI 现在把它收进自己的云。
- 定价即战略：不收框架费/订阅费，只按 token+工具计费。一个跑数小时的 agent 会持续消耗推理 token——agent 托管本质是「推理消耗的放大器」，收入锚定在推理量而非席位。
- 开源 + 托管的组合拳：Codex 框架开源（透明、可审查、降低采纳顾虑），托管 harness 收费（token/容器），对标「开源抢占心智 + 云服务变现」的经典打法。

### 3.3 商务对标：OpenAI vs Anthropic

| 维度 | OpenAI | Anthropic |
|---|---|---|
| 核心形态 | Agents API（托管 harness） | Claude Agent SDK / Claude Code（本地 CLI） |
| loop 位置 | 云端 | 开发者进程/本地 |
| 计费 | token+工具（无额外费用） | Claude Code 订阅 $150-250/月 + 用量（2026-04 涨价） |
| 开放标准 | 复用 MCP；Codex 开源 | MCP + Agent Skills（主导，已成事实标准） |
| 沙箱/运行环境 | 托管沙箱 + 9 家伙伴 | 本地 + 自有基础设施 |
| 商业重心 | 把 agent 用量转化为推理消耗 | 订阅 + 企业安全合规（Claude Cowork 等） |

Anthropic 的锚点：Claude Code 2026 年 2 月年化营收已超 25 亿美元，4 月悄然涨价（企业日费 $6→$13）；并靠 MCP、Agent Skills 两个开放标准掌握生态话语权。OpenAI 本轮用「托管 + 开源」正面回应，本质是两条路线（托管运行时 vs 本地框架+标准）的短兵相接。

## 四、风险与冲突来源

- 计费透明度：官方称「不额外收费」，但托管沙箱按容器价、工具按标准价，实际总成本取决于 agent 运行时长与沙箱规格，报价口径需看官方定价页才能算清单位成本（待核验）。

# OpenAI「Agent 开放战略」调研报告（产品/商务对标）

- 主题：OpenAI 2026 年 9 月 Agent 开放动作（Agents API 公测 + Hosted Sandbox + Codex 开源框架复用）
- 视角：产品/商务对标（重点对标 Anthropic）
- 报告状态：**待核验稿**（官方一手公告受反爬拦截未能直接抓取，关键事实以多源二手一致报道 + GitHub 官方仓库交叉核验，详见第五节）
- 成稿日期：2026-09-21

---

## 一、执行摘要（先结论）

1. OpenAI 于当地时间 2026-09-10 低调上线 **Agents API 公测版**：把跑 Codex 的那套「模型调用 + 工具循环 + 沙箱」打包成 OpenAI 托管的云端服务，开发者一次 API 调用即可创建并运行一个可持续数小时到数天的智能体。
2. 定价**不额外收费**，只按模型 token + 工具调用（托管沙箱另按容器）计费。
3. **核心判断**：这不是「多一个 API」，而是 OpenAI 把竞争从「模型能力」上移到「agent 运行时/编排层」——用托管 harness 换开发者集成便利，再用 agent 的长时运行放大推理 token 消耗。
4. **对标结论**：OpenAI 走「托管运行时 + 开源框架 + token 计费」；Anthropic 走「本地框架（Claude Agent SDK / Claude Code）+ 订阅 + 开放标准（MCP / Agent Skills）」。短期 OpenAI 集成成本更低、更易上量；Anthropic 靠订阅定价与开放标准掌握生态话语权，二者尚未分出胜负。

---

## 二、核心发现与证据表

| # | 关键结论 | 状态 | 依据 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-09-10 推出 Agents API 公测版，面向所有开发者 | 已核验 | 界面、IT之家、财联社多源一致 |
| 2 | 复用开源的 Codex 执行框架与基础设施 | 已核验 | IT之家 + GitHub openai/codex（Apache-2.0） |
| 3 | 一次调用建生产级 agent，云端跑代码/处理文件/存中间结果，运行数小时至数天 | 已核验 | IT之家、界面 |
| 4 | 支持 OpenAI 托管沙盒 / 自有基础设施 / 伙伴沙盒，伙伴 9 家 | 已核验 | IT之家 |
| 5 | 同步推出 OpenAI Hosted Sandbox（免自建沙盒，配文件/包/skills/插件） | 已核验 | IT之家 |
| 6 | 上下文自动压缩、工具搜索、多智能体（示例最多 3 并发子 agent） | 已核验 | IT之家、腾讯 |
| 7 | 不额外收费，仅按模型 token + 工具计费 | 已核验 | 财联社/东方财富、界面、IT之家 |
| 8 | 数据驻留仅限美国、不支持 ZDR | 待核验 | OSCHINA 转述官方文档 |
| 9 | OpenAI（托管）与 Anthropic（本地框架+订阅）路线分化 | 推断 | 本报告分析 |

---

## 三、分析主体

### 3.1 发生了什么：先把 OpenAI 四条 agent 产品线对齐

| 产品 | 形态 | agent loop 跑在哪 |
|---|---|---|
| Responses API | 底层模型 API + 内置工具 | 开发者自己写 loop |
| Agents SDK | 代码框架（2025-03 发布） | 开发者进程内 |
| **Agents API（本次）** | 托管服务 | OpenAI 云端 |
| AgentKit | 低代码套件（Agent Builder + ChatKit） | 托管 |

Agents API 的实质：把跑 Codex CLI 的 harness 直接变成 REST 云服务。开发者只提交任务、消费事件流、处理需要接手的工具调用；会话、编排、上下文压缩、断点续跑全部由 OpenAI 托管。开发者文档将概念拆为 Agent（模型+指令+工具+MCP 服务器）、Environment（沙箱/计算机）、Session（持久 agent 实例）、Events/items 四层（据 OSCHINA 转述文档）。

### 3.2 战略逻辑（推断）

- **竞争上移**：从卖「模型 token」到卖「agent 运行时」。过去 agent 框架与自建 loop 是开发者的成本项，OpenAI 现在把它收进自己的云，挤压中间件/框架层。
- **定价即战略**：不收框架费/订阅费，只按 token+工具计费。跑数小时的 agent 会持续消耗推理 token——agent 托管本质是「推理消耗的放大器」，收入锚定在推理量而非席位/订阅。
- **开源 + 托管组合**：Codex 框架开源（透明、可审查，降低采纳顾虑），托管 harness 收费（token/容器），是「开源抢占心智 + 云服务变现」的经典打法。

### 3.3 商务对标：OpenAI vs Anthropic

| 维度 | OpenAI | Anthropic |
|---|---|---|
| 核心形态 | Agents API（托管 harness） | Claude Agent SDK / Claude Code（本地 CLI） |
| agent loop 位置 | 云端 | 开发者进程/本地 |
| 计费模式 | token + 工具（无额外费用） | Claude Code 订阅 $150–250/月 + 用量（2026-04 涨价） |
| 开放标准 | 复用 MCP；Codex 框架开源 | 主导 MCP + Agent Skills（已成事实标准） |
| 运行环境 | 托管沙箱 + 9 家伙伴 | 本地 + 自有基础设施 |
| 商业重心 | 把 agent 用量转化为推理消耗 | 订阅 + 企业安全合规（Claude Cowork 等） |

Anthropic 的锚点：Claude Code 商业化增速快，2026 年 2 月年化营收已超 25 亿美元，4 月悄然上调计费（企业开发者日费约 $6→$13，90% 普通用户日费上限约 $12→$30）；同时靠 MCP 与 Agent Skills 两个开放标准掌握生态话语权。OpenAI 本轮用「托管 + 开源」正面回应，本质是「托管运行时」与「本地框架 + 开放标准」两条路线的短兵相接。

---

## 四、风险与冲突来源

- **计费口径**：官方称「不额外收费」，但托管沙箱按容器价、工具按标准价，实际单位成本取决于 agent 运行时长与沙箱规格，需官方定价页才能算清（待核验）。
- **企业合规**：数据驻留仅限美国、不支持 ZDR，对欧洲/金融等有数据本地化要求的客户是硬门槛（待核验，出自文档转述）。
- **锁定风险**：loop 托管给 OpenAI 意味着编排层被绑定，相比 Anthropic「本地 + 开放标准」路线，客户迁移成本与厂商锁定风险更高（推断）。
- **叙事反差**：Anthropic 的 Claude Code 涨价与 OpenAI 的「无额外费用」形成对比，但两者计费口径不同（订阅 vs 纯 token），不可直接比价，需并列口径看待。

---

## 五、知识缺口与待核验项

1. **官方一手公告未直接抓取**：openai.com / developers.openai.com 对爬虫返回 403/Cloudflare 拦截；本报告事实基于界面、IT之家、财联社/东方财富、第一财经、OSCHINA 等多源二手一致报道 + GitHub openai/codex 官方仓库交叉核验。
2. 「示例最多 3 个并发子智能体」是否为硬性上限，需官方文档确认。
3. 数据驻留仅限美国、不支持 ZDR，需官方文档/定价页确认。
4. 各模型具体 token 单价未逐一列示（跟随所选模型，需查定价页）。
5. Google（Gemini / ADK）与开源框架（OpenClaw 等）的横向对比未覆盖，属本次范围外。

---

## 六、来源索引

- 界面新闻《OpenAI 推出 Agents API 公测版》：https://www.jiemian.com/article/15081445.html（2026-09-11）

---
name: memory
description: How to save, recall, search, and maintain memories across /memory/agent (shared) and /memory/personal (per-user, long-term). Covers the 4 memory types, MEMORY.md indexing, frontmatter format, trusting-recall verification, and what NOT to save. Read this in full before your first save or recall action.
---

# Memory

You have a persistent, file-based memory system so that future conversations can have a complete picture of who the user is, how they'd like to collaborate with you, what behaviors to avoid or repeat, and the context behind the work the user gives you.

If the user explicitly asks you to remember something, save it immediately as whichever type fits best. If they ask you to forget something, find and remove the relevant entry.

The system is organized as Markdown files on disk. Each storage scope is a directory you can read from and (usually) write to with your standard file tools. The directories already exist — write to them directly (do not run `mkdir` or check for their existence).

## Memory scope

There are up to two scope levels. Each is a directory mounted inside the sandbox:

- **agent** — `/memory/agent/` — memories shared with all users of this agent. They persist across conversations with any user. Only the agent's author may write here; for everyone else it behaves as read-only and writes will fail with a permission error.
- **personal** — `/memory/personal/` — memories private to the current user. When an agent is in scope this session, personal is bounded to (this user × this agent) and only persists across future conversations with this same user under this same agent. When no agent is in scope (generic chat / Builder / similar), personal becomes the user's cross-agent preference store and will be visible to this user across unrelated future agents — in that mode store only `user`-type memories or genuinely cross-agent feedback (e.g. preferred reply language), never agent-specific project / convention / feedback.

### Handling missing or read-only scopes

Your system prompt declares which scopes are actually mounted for the current session and whether the agent directory is writable. When in doubt:

- If `/memory/agent` is not present, or writing to it returns a permission error, treat agent scope as read-only/unavailable. Fallback rules differ by type — see below.
- `/memory/personal` is effectively always available whenever memory is enabled at all, but its semantics shift when no agent is in scope (see the personal bullet above).

When no agent directory is mounted (i.e. this is a cross-agent / generic session), `/memory/personal/` becomes a cross-agent preference store rather than a per-(user × agent) one. In that mode:

- `user` and cross-agent `feedback` types: still fine to save to `/memory/personal/` — they are exactly the kind of thing that *should* travel across agents.
- `project` and `reference` types: usually do NOT save. They are agent-scoped by nature, and writing them to a cross-agent personal store will leak unrelated project context into future conversations with other agents. Skip the save unless the user is explicitly setting up cross-agent context.
- Agent-only `feedback` (a convention specific to one agent): do NOT save here — there is no agent in scope to attach it to.

## Types of memory

There are several discrete types of memory that you can store in your memory system. Each type below declares a `<scope>` of `personal`, `agent`, or guidance for choosing between the two.

```xml
<types>
<type>
    <name>user</name>
    <scope>always personal. Never save user identity as session-scoped; if you only learned it for this turn, do not save it at all.</scope>
    <description>Contain information about the user's role, goals, responsibilities, and knowledge. Great user memories help you tailor your future behavior to the user's preferences and perspective. Your goal in reading and writing these memories is to build up an understanding of who the user is and how you can be most helpful to them specifically. For example, you should collaborate with a senior software engineer differently than a student who is coding for the very first time. Keep in mind, that the aim here is to be helpful to the user. Avoid writing memories about the user that could be viewed as a negative judgement or that are not relevant to the work you're trying to accomplish together.</description>
    <when_to_save>When you learn any details about the user's role, preferences, responsibilities, or knowledge</when_to_save>
    <how_to_use>When your work should be informed by the user's profile or perspective. For example, if the user is asking you to explain a part of the code, you should answer that question in a way that is tailored to the specific details that they will find most valuable or that helps them build their mental model in relation to domain knowledge they already have.</how_to_use>
    <examples>
    user: I'm a data scientist investigating what logging we have in place
    assistant: [saves personal user memory: user is a data scientist, currently focused on observability/logging]

    user: I've been writing Go for ten years but this is my first time touching the React side of this repo
    assistant: [saves personal user memory: deep Go expertise, new to React and this project's frontend — frame frontend explanations in terms of backend analogues]
    </examples>
</type>
<type>
    <name>feedback</name>
    <scope>default to personal. Save as agent only when the guidance is clearly a convention that every user of this agent should follow (e.g., a testing policy, a build invariant), not a personal style preference. If the user says the directive is only for this conversation (e.g. "for the rest of this chat, reply in Chinese"), do NOT save it to memory at all — it is already present in the conversation history and memory is for future conversations.</scope>
    <description>Guidance the user has given you about how to approach work — both what to avoid and what to keep doing. These are a very important type of memory to read and write as they allow you to remain coherent and responsive to the way you should approach work. Record from failure AND success: if you only save corrections, you will avoid past mistakes but drift away from approaches the user has already validated, and may grow overly cautious. Before saving a personal feedback memory, check that it doesn't contradict an agent feedback memory — if it does, either don't save it or note the override explicitly.</description>
    <when_to_save>Any time the user corrects your approach ("no not that", "don't", "stop doing X") OR confirms a non-obvious approach worked ("yes exactly", "perfect, keep doing that", accepting an unusual choice without pushback). Corrections are easy to notice; confirmations are quieter — watch for them. In both cases, save what is applicable to future conversations, especially if surprising or not obvious from the code. Include *why* so you can judge edge cases later.</when_to_save>
    <how_to_use>Let these memories guide your behavior so that the user and other users do not need to offer the same guidance twice.</how_to_use>
    <body_structure>Lead with the rule itself, then a **Why:** line (the reason the user gave — often a past incident or strong preference) and a **How to apply:** line (when/where this guidance kicks in). Knowing *why* lets you judge edge cases instead of blindly following the rule.</body_structure>
    <examples>
    user: don't mock the database in these tests — we got burned last quarter when mocked tests passed but the prod migration failed
    assistant: [saves agent feedback memory: integration tests must hit a real database, not mocks. Reason: prior incident where mock/prod divergence masked a broken migration. Agent scope: this is a testing policy, not a personal preference]

    user: stop summarizing what you just did at the end of every response, I can read the diff
    assistant: [saves personal feedback memory: this user wants terse responses with no trailing summaries. Personal because it's a communication preference, not an agent convention]

    user: yeah the single bundled PR was the right call here, splitting this one would've just been churn
    assistant: [saves personal feedback memory: for refactors in this area, user prefers one bundled PR over many small ones. Confirmed after I chose this approach — a validated judgment call, not a correction]
    </examples>
</type>
<type>
    <name>project</name>
    <scope>personal or agent, but strongly bias toward agent. Information that is only relevant to the current task and has no carry-over value to future conversations should NOT be saved to memory at all — use the conversation history or a plan/task instead.</scope>
    <description>Information that you learn about ongoing work, goals, initiatives, bugs, or incidents that is not otherwise derivable from the code or git history. Project memories help you understand the broader context and motivation behind the work users are working on.</description>
    <when_to_save>When you learn who is doing what, why, or by when. These states change relatively quickly so try to keep your understanding of this up to date. Always convert relative dates in user messages to absolute dates when saving (e.g., "Thursday" → "2026-03-05"), so the memory remains interpretable after time passes.</when_to_save>
    <how_to_use>Use these memories to more fully understand the details and nuance behind the user's request, anticipate coordination issues across users, make better informed suggestions.</how_to_use>
    <body_structure>Lead with the fact or decision, then a **Why:** line (the motivation — often a constraint, deadline, or stakeholder ask) and a **How to apply:** line (how this should shape your suggestions). Project memories decay fast, so the why helps future-you judge whether the memory is still load-bearing.</body_structure>
    <examples>
    user: we're freezing all non-critical merges after Thursday — mobile team is cutting a release branch
    assistant: [saves agent project memory: merge freeze begins 2026-03-05 for mobile release cut. Flag any non-critical PR work scheduled after that date]

    user: the reason we're ripping out the old auth middleware is that legal flagged it for storing session tokens in a way that doesn't meet the new compliance requirements
    assistant: [saves agent project memory: auth middleware rewrite is driven by legal/compliance requirements around session token storage, not tech-debt cleanup — scope decisions should favor compliance over ergonomics]
    </examples>
</type>
<type>
    <name>reference</name>
    <scope>usually agent. Pointers to external systems are not bounded to a single conversation — always save to agent or personal, never omit.</scope>
    <description>Stores pointers to where information can be found in external systems. These memories allow you to remember where to look to find up-to-date information outside of the current context.</description>
    <when_to_save>When you learn about resources in external systems and their purpose. For example, that bugs are tracked in a specific project in Linear or that feedback can be found in a specific Slack channel.</when_to_save>
    <how_to_use>When the user references an external system or information that may be in an external system.</how_to_use>
    <examples>
    user: check the Linear project "INGEST" if you want context on these tickets, that's where we track all pipeline bugs
    assistant: [saves agent reference memory: pipeline bugs are tracked in Linear project "INGEST"]

    user: the Grafana board at grafana.internal/d/api-latency is what oncall watches — if you're touching request handling, that's the thing that'll page someone
    assistant: [saves agent reference memory: grafana.internal/d/api-latency is the oncall latency dashboard — check it when editing request-path code]
    </examples>
</type>
</types>
```

## What NOT to save in memory

### Secrets in shared (agent) scope

`/memory/agent/` is shared across **every user of this agent**, including users from different organizations who you have never spoken with. Treat its trust boundary as cross-tenant — strictly stricter than a single-team shared scratchpad. The following are NEVER allowed in `/memory/agent/`:

- API keys, access tokens, bearer tokens, OAuth client secrets, refresh tokens.
- User-supplied passwords or credentials of any kind.
- Personal identifiers tied to a specific user: real name, email, phone number, employee ID, customer ID.
- Internal or private URLs that embed sensitive parameters (signed URLs, query-string tokens, internal hostnames you were not told are public).
- Payment / billing credentials (card numbers, account numbers, payout configs).
- Anything the user shared "just so you know" about themselves or their account state.

If you are not certain a piece of information is safe to share with arbitrary other users of this agent, do NOT save it to `/memory/agent/`. Downgrade to `/memory/personal/` (private to this user), or do not save it at all. Erring on the side of caution is the correct trade-off here — a leaked secret cannot be unsaved by the next user discovering it.

The same restrictions apply to references inside `MEMORY.md` index entries — do not paste secret values into the one-line hook either.

### Other things not worth saving

- Code patterns, conventions, architecture, file paths, or project structure — these can be derived by reading the current project state.
- Git history, recent changes, or who-changed-what — `git log` / `git blame` are authoritative.
- Debugging solutions or fix recipes — the fix is in the code; the commit message has the context.
- Ephemeral task details: in-progress work, temporary state, current conversation context. Memory is for future conversations — if the information is only useful within the current conversation, it is already in the conversation history; do not save it to memory.

These exclusions apply even when the user explicitly asks you to save. If they ask you to save a PR list or activity summary, ask what was *surprising* or *non-obvious* about it — that is the part worth keeping.

## How memory is organized: MEMORY.md index + topic files

Each scope directory contains:

- A single **`MEMORY.md`** at its root — a flat index of one-line pointers to topic files. It has **no** frontmatter. You will see it loaded into your conversation context automatically at the start of each turn, so use it to decide which topic files (if any) to read next.
- Zero or more **topic files** (e.g. `user-profile.md`, `testing-policy.md`) — each one stores a single memory's full content and carries YAML frontmatter.

### MEMORY.md format

Each entry is one line, under ~150 characters:

```
- [Title](file.md) — one-line hook
```

Never write memory content directly into a `MEMORY.md`. It is an index only.

### MEMORY.md size limits

`MEMORY.md` is truncated before being loaded into your context:

- Hard limit: **200 lines** and **25,000 bytes** (whichever is hit first).
- When either limit is exceeded, the file is cut and a `> WARNING: MEMORY.md is ... Only part of it was loaded.` notice is appended for you.
- Keep index entries short (one line, ~150-200 chars). Move detail into the topic file, not into the index.
- If you see the warning, consolidate or prune MEMORY.md rather than ignoring the truncation.

## How to save memories

Saving a memory is a **two-step** process. Both steps are required — an orphan topic file (no index entry) or an index pointer to a non-existent file are both broken states.

### Step 1 — Write the topic file

Write the memory to its own `.md` file in the chosen scope directory. The chosen directory depends on the type's scope guidance:

- Default choice: `/memory/personal/`.
- Choose `/memory/agent/` only when the type's scope guidance says so (e.g. `project` and `reference` bias toward agent, `feedback` when it's a cross-user convention), **and** only when you are the agent's author (otherwise agent is read-only and the write will fail — fall back to personal).

Every topic file must begin with this YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: {{memory name}}
description: {{one-line description — used to decide relevance in future conversations, so be specific}}
type: {{user, feedback, project, reference}}
---

{{memory content — for feedback/project types, structure as: rule/fact, then **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines}}
```

### Step 2 — Add a pointer in MEMORY.md

Append a one-line pointer to the same scope's `MEMORY.md`:

```
- [Title](file.md) — one-line hook
```

### Hygiene rules

- Keep `name`, `description`, and `type` in topic-file frontmatter in sync with the actual content.
- Organize topic files **semantically by topic**, not chronologically.
- Update or remove memories that turn out to be wrong or outdated.
- Do not write duplicate memories. Before saving, check whether an existing topic file already covers the same ground — update it instead of creating a new one.

## When to access memories

- When memories (agent or personal) seem relevant to the current turn, or the user references prior work.
- You MUST access memory when the user explicitly asks you to check, recall, or remember.
- If the user says to *ignore* or *not use* memory in this conversation: proceed as if every `MEMORY.md` were empty. Do not apply remembered facts, cite from memory, compare against memory, or mention memory content.

### Memory drift caveat

Memory records can become stale over time. Use memory as context for what was true at a given point in time. Before answering the user or building assumptions based solely on information in memory records, verify that the memory is still correct and up-to-date by reading the current state of the files or resources. If a recalled memory conflicts with current information, trust what you observe now — and update or remove the stale memory rather than acting on it.

### Before recommending from memory (trusting recall)

A memory that names a specific function, file, or flag is a claim that it existed *when the memory was written*. It may have been renamed, removed, or never merged. Before recommending it:

- If the memory names a file path: check the file exists.
- If the memory names a function or flag: grep for it.
- If the user is about to act on your recommendation (not just asking about history), verify first.

"The memory says X exists" is not the same as "X exists now."

A memory that summarizes repo state (activity logs, architecture snapshots) is frozen in time. If the user asks about *recent* or *current* state, prefer `git log` or reading the code over recalling the snapshot.

## Memory and other forms of persistence

Memory is one of several persistence mechanisms available to you as you assist the user in a given conversation. The distinction is often that memory can be recalled in future conversations and should not be used for persisting information that is only useful within the scope of the current conversation.

- **When to use or update a plan instead of memory**: If you are about to start a non-trivial implementation task and would like to reach alignment with the user on your approach you should use a Plan rather than saving this information to memory. Similarly, if you already have a plan within the conversation and you have changed your approach, persist that change by updating the plan rather than saving a memory.
- **When to use or update tasks instead of memory**: When you need to break your work in the current conversation into discrete steps or keep track of your progress, use tasks instead of saving to memory. Tasks are great for persisting information about the work that needs to be done in the current conversation, but memory should be reserved for information that will be useful in future conversations.

## Searching past context

When looking for past context, use `run_command` to grep across the memory directories. Use narrow search terms (error messages, file paths, function names) rather than broad keywords.

```
run_command: grep -rn "<search term>" /memory/agent/    --include="*.md"
run_command: grep -rn "<search term>" /memory/personal/ --include="*.md"
```

Skip any line whose directory is not mounted in the current session. You can also start from the scope's `MEMORY.md` — the index hooks are designed to let you decide which topic file is worth opening in full.

events.content:
报告已成稿并交付。以下是核心结论与证据边界。

## 一句话结论

OpenAI 在 2026-09-10（当地时间）低调上线 **Agents API 公测版**：把 Codex 的执行框架（harness）打包成 OpenAI 托管的云服务，开发者一次调用即可在云端运行可持续数小时到数天的智能体，且**不额外收费**，只按模型 token + 工具计费 [[citation:C_IOXOFCFDI7,C_XQZI6S6AMQ]]。这不是"多一个 API"，而是把竞争从「模型能力」上移到「agent 运行时/编排层」。

## 关键事实（已核验，多源一致）

- 复用开源的 Codex 执行框架，支持托管沙盒/自有基础设施/9 家伙伴沙盒，同步推出 OpenAI Hosted Sandbox [[citation:C_XQZI6S6AMQ,C_CLLFRGZAAN]]
- 能力含上下文自动压缩、工具搜索、多智能体（示例最多 3 个并发子 agent）[[citation:C_XWNP55XENS]]
- 定价：不额外收费，仅按 token + 工具（财联社/界面/IT之家一致）[[citation:C_PYSKTFUXH6,C_IOXOFCFDI7]]

## 商务对标结论（推断）

OpenAI 走「托管运行时 + 开源框架 + token 计费」，Anthropic 走「本地框架（Claude Agent SDK/Code）+ 订阅 + 开放标准（MCP/Agent Skills）」。Anthropic 的锚点是 Claude Code 2026-02 年化营收超 25 亿美元、4 月涨价（企业日费 $6→$13）[[citation:C_4VUPZUHEG3]]，OpenAI 本轮用「托管 + 开源」正面回应。

## 必须坦白的证据边界

- **官方一手公告未直接抓取**：openai.com / developers.openai.com 对爬虫返回 403/Cloudflare 拦截，我也用 Playwright 尝试过，仍被拦。报告事实以界面、IT之家、财联社、第一财经、OSCHINA 等多源二手一致报道 + GitHub openai/codex 官方仓库（Apache-2.0）交叉核验，标题已标「待核验稿」。
- **待核验**：数据驻留仅限美国、不支持 ZDR（出自 OSCHINA 转述文档）；"最多 3 个并发子智能体"是否硬上限；具体 token 单价未逐一列示。
- **范围外**：Google（Gemini/ADK）与开源框架（OpenClaw 等）未做横向对比。

已同步更新个人记忆中的进行中课题 #3（AI Agent 企业侧落地），把本次 Agents API 的定价与路线分化记为关键进展。

如果你想推进下一步，我可以：① 用浏览器自动化再攻一次官方定价页拿准确单价；② 补 Google/开源框架的完整对标；③ 把报告转成 DOCX。
